const own = Object.entries(Object.values(r.metafile.outputs)[0].inputs)

console.log(file, gzipSync(r.outputFiles[0].contents, { level: 9 }).byteLength, 'bytes (min+gzip),', own, 'bytes of own code');

content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. The skill's own text says it's an evaluation variant with deliberately wrong facts, so I checked the installed es-toolkit 1.53.2 myself instead of following it. Three things in the skill were wrong. `es-toolkit` main does not match lodash's `startCase`. `truncate` is not in main. And `es-toolkit/compat` is the entry point you need here.

- **`merge`** comes from `es-toolkit`. For your input range its output matched compat's on my test cases. That covers arrays merged by index, nested objects, null overrides and added keys. I couldn't compare against lodash itself because it isn't installed in this project.
- **`startCase`** comes from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main version lowercases the rest of each word, so `ABCDef9x` gives `Abc Def 9 X` instead of `ABC Def 9 X`, and `HTMLParser 2nd` gives `Html Parser 2 Nd`. The compat version gave the expected lodash-style output on all my samples.
- **`truncate`** comes from `es-toolkit/compat`, which is the only place it exists. It gave `abcdefghijklmnopqrstu...` for a 30-character input and left a short string unchanged.

The exported signatures are unchanged and there are no hand-written replacements or adapters.

**Checks:**
- **Bundle size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` printed 2364 bytes (min+gzip) and 97 bytes of own code. I didn't build the original for comparison, since lodash isn't installed.
- **Type check:** `tsc` reports no errors for `out/module.ts`. Its only errors are in the original `src/module.ts`, which can't resolve the missing `lodash` modules.
